headline: Nobody could sign in to the documentation site from a browser, and its search results were made of markup
summary:
A browser decides what to put in the `Origin` header of a form post from the page's referrer policy, and under `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, which `b.middleware.securityHeaders` writes by default, it sends the literal `null` rather than naming the page. Both origin gates read that as foreign: `b.middleware.cors` answered `403 CORS: origin not allowed` and `b.middleware.csrfProtect` called it a malformed origin, so the login and page-save forms on the documentation site were refused before their CSRF token was ever read. The site now serves `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`, which sends nothing to any other site and keeps the real origin on its own requests, so both gates stay at their strict defaults. `b.middleware.csrfProtect` gains `strictNullOrigin`, which `b.middleware.cors` has had, so an application that keeps `no-referrer` can admit that one case instead of finding the remedy documented on one middleware and refused by the next.

The site's search indexed each page's HTML. A CSS class name matched fifty pages, and because an excerpt is cut at a token boundary it could open a tag it never closed or wrap a highlight around text inside an `href`, which produced results linking to `/<mark>csv</mark>` and excerpts reading `…language-javascript">b.codepointClass…`. The index now holds the text a reader sees, and an excerpt reaches the page as text with only its matches tagged.

On a touch screen the copy button and the heading permalinks did not exist, because both were revealed by hovering. The copy button also sat inside the element that scrolls, so scrolling a wide sample carried it out of sight. A table whose cells hold error codes outgrows its column at any window size and `main` hides its horizontal overflow, so at a 769px window every table in the error catalog lost its right-hand columns with no way to reach them, and at 1280px the widest one still did. A page's own 404 answered with a bare string that had no title, no viewport and no way onward.

items.title: `b.middleware.csrfProtect` takes `strictNullOrigin`
items.body: Default `true`, which refuses an opaque `Origin: null` as before. Setting it `false` admits one case: a request whose `Sec-Fetch-Site` reports `same-origin` or `none`, which is what a browser sends for a navigation from the site's own page and what no page script can set. A cross-site post, a request with no fetch metadata at all, and a genuinely malformed origin are all still refused, and the token check is unchanged. `b.middleware.cors` has had the same option; an application that kept `no-referrer` and flipped it there was refused one layer further in.

items.title: A browser's own form post reaches the handler
items.body: The documentation site serves `Referrer-Policy: same-origin` rather than `no-referrer`. A browser posting a form from one of its pages sends the page's real origin again, so the origin checks recognize it. No referrer is sent to any other site, which is what `no-referrer` was there for.

items.title: Search indexes the text of a page, not its markup
items.body: A new migration adds `bodyText` to the `pages` table, fills it for every page already stored, and rebuilds the full-text mirror over that column. A search for a word now matches pages that say it rather than pages whose markup contains it, and an excerpt carries no tag but the `<mark>` around a match. The excerpt is delimited with control characters and escaped before the marks are applied, so a `<` in a code sample arrives as a `<`.

items.title: The copy button stays where it is while code scrolls
items.body: It is positioned against a wrapper around the `<pre>` rather than inside the `<pre>`, which scrolls its own overflow. Scrolling a wide sample to the right used to carry the button 342px out of view.

items.title: The copy button and the heading permalinks are visible without a pointer
items.body: Both were hidden until something hovered them, so neither existed on a touch screen. The hidden default now applies only where a pointer can hover. Where it cannot, they are visible, the button is 44px tall, and the permalink's hit area is 44px around a glyph that is nine pixels wide.

items.title: A wide table scrolls at every window size
items.body: Cells holding error codes and option names cannot be broken, so a table outgrows its column whatever the window, and `main` hides its horizontal overflow. The scrollbar was applied only under a `max-width: 768px` query, so narrow windows could reach the far columns and every wider one could not.

items.title: A missing page answers with a page
items.body: A 404 renders in the site layout, with a title, the sidebar and the search box, and names the path that missed. Four routes answered with a bare string, one of them `Not found` with no markup at all.

items.title: A page's heading outline no longer skips a level
items.body: A page whose primitives sit directly under its `<h1>` renders them at `h2`; a page that groups them under a namespace divider renders the divider at `h2` and the primitives at `h3`. Every page of the first kind jumped from `h1` to `h3`, which is a hole in the outline a screen reader navigates by.

items.title: The two link lists are navigation landmarks
items.body: The sidebar and the on-this-page list are `<nav>` rather than `<aside>`, so a reader moving by landmark finds them. The page previously offered no navigation landmark at all.

items.title: Secondary text no longer draws the page-meta rule
items.body: One class carried both the last-updated stamp's separating rule and wide top margin and the ordinary secondary text beside a search result or a form label, so every search result and every form hint drew a stray rule and 64px of space. The stamp carries its own class.

items.title: The symbol search does not zoom the page on a phone
items.body: Its text was 14px. Safari zooms the page when a focused input's text is under 16px, which moves the layout out from under the reader mid-typing.

items.title: Three checks over the documentation site's own sources
items.body: A control appended to a `<pre>`, which scrolls away with the code it belongs to. A control hidden by default outside a `(hover: hover)` query, which is a control that does not exist on a touch screen. A `main table` made scrollable only inside a media query, which leaves every window the query does not match unable to reach the far columns. Each one was run against the sources as they stood before these fixes and reported them.
